chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'People will miss their Imam. He attends the seasons (of Hajj), so he sees them, but they do not see him.'

key_terms.الْمَوَاسِمَ: The seasons (specifically referring to Hajj seasons)
key_terms.يَفْقِدُ: They will miss/lose (the sense of his presence)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam's presence during Hajj signify in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghaybah* illustrates the theological concept of the Hidden Imam's ubiquity during pilgrimage seasons, where he observes the faithful while they remain unaware of his presence. It underscores the Shia belief in the Imam's continuous spiritual guidance and physical proximity despite his concealment, reinforcing the idea that the community has not been abandoned. This specific description serves as a key evidence for the reality of the Minor Occultation and the Imam's active role in the world.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (14) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya from Ja’far bin Muhammad from Iss’haq bin Muhammad from Yahya bin al-Muthanna from Abdullah bin Bukayr that Obayd bin Zurara
had heard Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) saying: “People will miss their imam. He attends the seasons of hajj. He sees the people but they do not see him.”
